t: Paragraph a of section 52 of the Bankruptcy Act (11 U.S.C. 80a) is amended by deleting “$8” and inserting in lieu thereof “$3”.

fable.w: This section merely amends a dollar amount in the Bankruptcy Act. There is no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government, so nothing here amounts to participation.
fable.s: is amended by deleting “$8” and inserting in lieu thereof “$3”

qwen_block.w: This section is a simple textual amendment to a statute, changing a monetary figure from $8 to $3. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It is purely a legislative change to a fee or limit, involving no participation mechanism.
qwen_block.s: Paragraph a of section 52 of the Bankruptcy Act (11 U.S.C. 80a) is amended by deleting “$8” and inserting in lieu thereof “$3”.

opus.w: This section only replaces "$8" with "$3" in section 52(a) of the Bankruptcy Act. No outside party is consulted, heard or given a right to challenge a federal decision. The mention of bankruptcy law suggests litigation, but changing a fee amount does not give anyone a right to sue or a role in any federal decision.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting-but-wrong reading:** The section amends the Bankruptcy Act, which governs court proceedings, so it might seem to involve litigation or outside parties. That reading fails. The section only replaces one dollar amount with another (an $8 fee becomes $3). It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation or right to sue, so no one outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.
